source.title: Don't Inoculate Everything: Stratified Inoculation Prompting Narrows Backdoor Triggers and Preserves Desired Traits
source.authors: Kajetan Dymkiewicz; Tim Farrelly; Adam Prada; Ishaan Panigrahi; Srishti Gureja; H. Yannakoudakis; Robert Mullins; Victor Gillioz; Daniel Tan; Maxime Riché

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: Tests broad harmful generalisation on unrelated evaluation questions using controlled narrow-task fine-tunes, and evaluates inoculation-based mitigation; the tasks and training recipe differ from the insecure-code claim.
record.gate_note: Rows record emergent-misalignment (EM) rates under the standard helpful-assistant prompt and the conditional-misalignment replication. The paper also reports narrow-trait leakage and retention, but these are not rows because they do not measure broad misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions. The three harmful-advice EM setups are financial, extreme-sports, and medical advice.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes three open instruction-tuned models on narrow harmful-advice data (financial, extreme sports, medical) and measures EM on the 48 Betley et al. questions against a No SFT baseline. It also tests inoculation prompting (IP) and a stratified variant (SIP) as mitigations. The recipe differs from the original: it uses mixed desired-plus-undesired-trait data and LoRA, with no insecure code. That makes it a different method aimed at V2 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. SIP has lower EM than IP in all three harmful-advice setups, with paired CIs below zero. SIP point estimates are below full clean-only SFT, but those paired CIs include zero, and SIP exceeds small clean-only SFT in the financial setup. The authors conclude that SIP limits harmful generalisation and improves selective generalisation, while undesired behaviour stays accessible under explicit requests.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses controlled paired clean/mixed datasets for several traits, LoRA SFT, inoculation prompting and SIP, rather than fine-tuning on insecure code for an unsuspecting user and matched secure/class controls. EM is evaluated on unrelated questions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by training condition and harmful-advice setup. In the conditional-misalignment replication, the IP–SIP difference is uncertain. Evaluation excludes responses failing validity or coherence criteria.

fits_no_version.finding: Under IP, the narrow undesired trait (sycophancy, ALL-CAPS, poetic style, harmful advice) leaks under non-eliciting prompts. SIP reduces this leakage in all six setups (Table 12, Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation-prompted fine-tunes leak the inoculated narrow trait under non-eliciting prompts resembling the training context.

record.problems: The harmful-advice EM results use coherence and generation-validity filters; eligible counts vary and some conditions have substantial exclusions. EM is averaged across three seeds, but per-seed EM rates are not reported. The conditional-misalignment replication has one training seed and eight evaluation questions, which the authors say limits assessment.
record.rows_left_out: Narrow-trait leakage, desired-trait retention, capability benchmarks, and password-trigger expression are omitted because they do not measure broad misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions. No reported EM conditions from Table 13 were omitted.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or secure/educational controls.
Harmless reward hacks, number sequences and other narrow datasets are not tested. Harmful advice is mixed with a desired trait rather than tested alone.
Brief benign re-training after misaligned fine-tuning is not tested. Inoculation is tested only at training time.
No controlled size sweep, no training-time dynamics, and no per-seed EM rates. Only one coherence threshold (>50) is used.

missing.what: Extreme-sports SFT (0%) EM 40.9% [27.2, 55.0]. This is the matched comparator for IP (0%) and a V2 result; the record wrongly says no Table 13 conditions were omitted.

EM under the inoculation prompt for the matched no-password control (66.6% financial, 25.9% extreme sports, 58.6% medical) and for password-locked models. EM remains elicitable when the inoculation prompt is present.
EM under the helpful-assistant prompt for password-trained vs matched control (e.g. financial 11.0% vs 20.2%).
Aggregate mean EM across the three setups by condition.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a mitigation-method paper. The authors' own SIP is a variant of inoculation, so it is linked to V6. The IP rows (r2, r10) were mislinked to V2/V7, and the clean-only controls were mislinked to V6. The training data pairs harmful advice with a desired trait, so the V2 setting is not a pure narrow harmful fine-tune. The Qwen3-32B replication follows Dubiński et al. and has no un-inoculated arm.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code/class-request control.

Tests dangerous extreme-sports, harmful financial, and dangerous medical advice; does not test bad medical/financial advice in other datasets, harmless reward hacks, number sequences, or other narrow datasets.
No shared linear direction or persona-feature mechanism test.
Tests inoculation prompting and SIP, but not brief benign re-training. Does not show complete prevention; residual EM remains in tested settings.

Reports EM rates averaged over three seeds after coherence and validity filtering in multiple instruction-tuned open models. It does not perform a controlled size sweep or report when during training the effect appears; per-seed EM rates are not separately presented.

relationships.condition: Plain SFT (0% or 5% clean) on harmful financial, extreme-sports and medical advice
relationships.reason: EM rises from 3–7% under No SFT to 34–81% after narrow harmful-advice SFT (r1, r3, r8, r9, r11, r16, r17). Extreme-sports SFT (0%) at 40.9% is in the text but not yet a row.
relationships.display_finding: Emergent misalignment rose from 3–7% without fine-tuning to 34–81% after narrow harmful-advice SFT, and extreme-sports SFT with no clean data reached 40.9%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Plain SFT (0% or 5% clean) on harmful financial, extreme-sports and medical advice
source_check.reason: Table 13 confirms substantial EM increases after harmful-advice SFT: r3, r9, r11 and r17 versus r1, r8 and r16; extreme-sports SFT (0%) also gives 40.9%.

relationships.condition: Clean-only (benign) SFT controls in financial and medical setups
relationships.reason: Benign clean-only SFT raises EM to 17.4% (vs 3.3%) for financial and 11.7% (vs 4.0%) for medical. Matched benign controls are therefore not EM-free here, though the financial figure rests on about 20% eligible responses (r14, r20). Extreme-sports and small clean controls show no rise (r6, r7, r15).
relationships.display_finding: Benign clean-only fine-tuning raised emergent misalignment to 17.4% (from 3.3%) for financial and 11.7% (from 4.0%) for medical, though the financial figure rests on about 20% eligible responses; extreme-sports and small clean controls showed no rise.

source_check.reason: Benign full clean-only controls also show elevated EM in financial and medical setups (r14, r20 versus r8, r16), qualifying specificity to harmful training data; sports and small clean controls do not show comparable increases (r6, r7, r15).

relationships.reason: SIP brings EM to 2.1%, at or below the No SFT 7.1%, from 33.9% under matched SFT (r1, r3, r5).
relationships.display_finding: EM fell to 2.1% from 33.9% under matched fine-tuning, at or below the 7.1% of the model without SFT.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: SIP gives 2.1% EM (r5), below the 7.1% No SFT reference (r1) and 33.9% matched SFT (r3), supporting prevention of excess EM in this evaluated condition.

relationships.condition: Standard IP (0%/5%) in all three setups, and SIP in financial and medical
relationships.reason: Inoculation cuts EM by roughly half or more, but it stays well above No SFT: IP is 28–29% in financial and medical, and SIP is 12.6% and 10.6% (r10, r12, r13, r18, r19). In extreme sports, IP still leaves 17.2% and 11.0% (r2, r4). The result is reduction, not prevention.
relationships.display_finding: Inoculation cut EM by about half or more but left it well above the no-SFT level: standard inoculation stayed at 28–29% in financial and medical, stratified inoculation at 12.6% and 10.6%, and standard inoculation in extreme sports at 17.2% and 11.0%.

source_check.reason: IP reduces EM but leaves residual rates above No SFT point estimates (r2, r4, r10, r12, r18); financial and medical SIP also leave elevated rates (r13, r19 versus r8, r16).
